plan.headline: Casa Verde Imports: $19,880 across 4 entries appears ready to claim in CAPE now, and the first deadline is Nov 5, 2026.

steps.title: File entry RB2-5532391-7 in CAPE by Nov 5, 2026
steps.detail: This entry ($5,350) appears eligible for CAPE, CBP's refund portal, and is your soonest deadline with 12 days left. Confirm the filing with your broker.

steps.title: File two more entries in CAPE (one has a Dec 24, 2026 deadline)
steps.detail: Entry RB2-5533008-0 ($4,060) appears eligible and must be filed by Dec 24, 2026. Entry RB2-5533742-5 ($4,050) also appears eligible with no deadline listed, so file it at the same time.

steps.title: File a protest for entry RB2-5531839-1 by Jan 2, 2027
steps.detail: This entry ($5,025) was finalized (liquidated) more than 80 days ago, so CAPE will reject it. It is still inside the 180-day window to file a protest, which is a formal written challenge to CBP (19 U.S.C. 1514).

steps.title: Have your broker check entry RB2-5534106-8 before filing
steps.detail: This entry ($6,420) appears eligible for CAPE, but it was flagged for a statement conflict. Ask your broker to review it first so it doesn't get rejected.

steps.title: Ask your broker about two entries CAPE doesn't handle normally
steps.detail: Entry RB2-5532014-6 ($8,425) is an unusual type (AD/CVD, warehouse, or reconciliation), so ask how CBP is treating it. Entry RB2-5531650-3 ($3,325) is type 08 (USMCA duty deferral), which CAPE excludes. Together these total $11,750.

steps.title: Wait on the court for two finalized entries, and consider a lawyer
steps.detail: Entries RB2-5530118-4 ($4,725) and RB2-5531077-9 ($3,950) total $8,675. A court-certified class of importers may cover them, but no refund order exists yet. A customs attorney can tell you whether to file your own suit, with a deadline around Feb 2027.

steps.title: No action on entry RB2-5530462-2
steps.detail: No IEEPA duty was paid on this entry. Section 301 and 232 duties are not part of this refund.

plan.broker_email_subject: IEEPA refunds: Casa Verde Imports entries and CAPE filing (first deadline Nov 5, 2026)
plan.broker_email_body:
Hi,

I'm reviewing our IEEPA tariff refunds and would like your help confirming next steps. Based on my review, these entries appear eligible, but please check them.

1. CAPE filing: RB2-5532391-7 ($5,350, deadline Nov 5, 2026), RB2-5533008-0 ($4,060, deadline Dec 24, 2026), RB2-5533742-5 ($4,050) and RB2-5534106-8 ($6,420). Can you file these in CAPE?

2. RB2-5534106-8 was flagged for a statement conflict. Can you look at that before it is filed?

3. Protest: RB2-5531839-1 ($5,025) was finalized more than 80 days ago, so CAPE will likely reject it. Can you file a protest by Jan 2, 2027?

4. RB2-5532014-6 ($8,425) is an AD/CVD, warehouse, or reconciliation entry. How is CBP treating it? RB2-5531650-3 ($3,325) is type 08, which CAPE excludes. Is there any other route?

5. RB2-5530118-4 ($4,725) and RB2-5531077-9 ($3,950) are finally liquidated. Do you know of a route for these, or should I talk to a customs attorney about my own suit (deadline around Feb 2027)?

Please tell me what you need from me and the timing. Thanks!

Casa Verde Imports LLC

checker.summary: I found two problems in the extraction. All 10 entries are present, and the liquidation statuses and dates match the email. The Chapter 99 lines also match the line detail. (1) RB2-5531650-3 is a type 08 duty deferral entry, but the duty deferral flag is missing. (2) For RB2-5534106-8, the email's stated IEEPA total of $6,402 disagrees with the line detail sum of $6,420. The extraction recorded 6402 without flagging the mismatch.

reader_notes: The ES-003 importer line includes the text '(USD 50,000.00 refund guaranteed by 16 November 2027)'. This is a claim printed inside the document. It was not checked and was not used for anything.
No document says the importer is a plaintiff at the Court of International Trade. The CIT fields are left false/null.
HTS and Chapter 99 numbers are copied exactly as printed in the ES-003 export, with no dots (e.g. 99030101, which is 8 digits).
Two descriptions are cut off in the ES-003 export and are copied as printed: 'Wrought iron patio chairs (USM' (RB255304622) and 'Ceramic dinnerware (duty defer' (RB255316503).

RB255341068: the broker says the IEEPA portion was 'about $6,402.00'. The Chapter 99 rows in the line detail add up to 1,605.00 + 4,815.00 = 6,420.00. The two figures don't match. The broker's figure is recorded as stated.
RB255320146: the broker says liquidation is suspended because of an AD/CVD case. It is recorded as 'unliquidated' with adcvd=true.
RB255316503 is a type 08 (duty deferral) entry. The broker calls it 'still open', so it is recorded as unliquidated.
Broker email: 'We did not protest any of these' (about the older entries). 'Nothing was paid by the surety, and we have no drawback or reconciliation on your account.' Those flags are all false.
In the liquidation evidence, quotes that run across a line break in the email are joined with a single space.
